s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of oral and skin lesions with abdominal discomfort and difficulty eating, associated with a renal mass and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Sudden warty growths over the lips
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in the axillae, posterior neck, periumbilical region, and groin folds
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms with papillomatous appearance
key_facts: 70-year-old woman
Sudden onset of oral lesions
Difficulty eating
6-month history of vague abdominal discomfort
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in multiple areas
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms
Large left-sided renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on abdominal CT
Necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing superior vena cava compression on thorax CT
Invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation on radiologically guided biopsy of renal mass

shortlist.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by tylosis and esophageal cancer, with oral lesions and palmoplantar keratoderma, matching the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Tylosis with oesophageal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Howel-Evans syndrome, with a strong association between tylosis, oral lesions, and esophageal cancer

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation on biopsy

shortlist.label: Muir-Torre syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: A subtype of Lynch syndrome with skin lesions and increased risk of various cancers, including urothelial carcinoma

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Focal squamous differentiation in the renal mass biopsy, suggesting possible squamous cell carcinoma component

raw.rationale: The combination of oral and skin lesions (papillomatosis and verrucous plaques) along with internal malignancy (urothelial carcinoma) is characteristic of Muir-Torre syndrome, a subtype of Lynch syndrome that involves sebaceous neoplasms and visceral cancers.

rejected.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
rejected.why: It primarily involves tylosis (thickening of the skin on the palms and soles) and oesophageal cancer, which doesn't fully match the patient's presentation of renal mass and specific skin lesions.

rejected.label: Tylosis with oesophageal cancer
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings do not include oesophageal cancer, and the skin manifestations are not limited to tylosis.

rejected.label: Urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has urothelial carcinoma, this diagnosis alone does not account for the dermatological findings and other systemic manifestations.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's presentation includes squamous differentiation in the renal mass, but the full spectrum of her symptoms, including specific skin and oral lesions, is more indicative of Muir-Torre syndrome than isolated squamous cell carcinoma.
